title: dcat catalogue manifest
description: The catalogues `dcat generate` produces and `dcat validate` checks. Read by the tool, and by an editor before the tool ever runs.

$comment.description: Prose about the manifest as a whole. A string or an array of lines.

catalogs.description: One entry per catalogue. An empty array generates nothing, which a scheduled job would read as success.

$comment.description: Prose about this entry — why this package, why this version line.

package.description: A package id to resolve from the configured NuGet sources.

version.description: Which release of `package`: an exact version, "latest" (latest stable) or "latest-any" (including prereleases). Defaults to "latest".

source.description: Which configured feed to resolve `package` from, by name or URL. Defaults to every enabled source.

nupkg.description: A .nupkg already on disk, relative to this manifest. Its .nuspec names the source unless sourceName/sourceVersion say otherwise.

projects.description: Projects that produce analyzers, relative to this manifest. They must already be built; nothing here builds them. Several when rules are split across projects, as an analyzer and its code fixes often are.

configuration.description: Which configuration of `projects` to read. Defaults to "Release".

assemblies.description: Analyzer assemblies already on disk, relative to this manifest. Several when a vendor splits its rules across them.

namespace.description: The namespace the generated catalogue declares.

container.description: The static class holding the rules. A name ending in "Rule" also names the category class: SonarRule gives SonarCategory.

output.description: Where the generated C# is written, relative to this manifest.

language.description: Which language's analyzers to read out of a package. Selecting one EXCLUDES the others rather than keeping only its folder, because most rules often sit in a language-neutral assembly.

sourceName.description: What to record as the source. Defaults to the package's own id, the project's assembly name, or the first assembly's name.

sourceVersion.description: What to record as the source's release. Defaults to the package's version, the project's declared Version, or the first assembly's. Worth setting when a source on disk keeps a version that stands still while its rules move.

allOf.$comment: version and source describe a feed, and mean nothing for a source on disk.
A feed states its own name and release; overriding them would record a provenance the package never claimed.
configuration selects among a project's build outputs, and nothing else has any.
